text.p: National Foods Ltd managing director Max Ould said on Thursday that Asian investor Camerlin had sold its stake of about 10 percent in the milk and fruit juice company.
Ould told Reuters that the Camerlin sale was handled by broker BZW Australia earlier in the afternoon and the stock distributed between a wide range of institutions.
He said he was not aware that Camerlin was intending to sell but knew the Malaysian-listed group had been reassessing its investment for some time.
"They (Camerlin) have just phone me to advise that they have sold and I have just spoken to BZW and they have advised me that they did place the shares with a range of institutions," Ould said.
"I was aware they (Camerlin) were reassessing their stake but I wasn't too sure which way they were going to go."
Ould said Camerlin and the other major Asian investor, Hong Kong's Mingly Corp, had significant stakes.
"They both continued to buy over the last 12 months and they are both sitting at around 10 or slightly in excess of 10 percent.
"So it is a natural strategic assessment, what do you want to do? Do you go forward or do you just sit there? And I think Camerlin did not want to be a passive player," Ould said.
The 25 million Camlerin shares were traded mid-afternoon in two parcels by BZW at A$1.95 each, four cents below the closing price and 10 cents below the record high struck on Wednesday.
The company was expected to announce "some fairly good results" with its 1996/97 (July-June) profit statement.
"I think the market will be satisfied," he said.
National Foods achieved a 1995/96 net profit of A$22.7 million and forecast in March this year that the 1996/97 result was likely to be higher.
